newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan says to allow HK protest ship to dock.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan says to allow HK protest ship to dock.

text.p: Taiwan said on Thursday it would allow a Hong Kong ship that ended a fatal protest trip to an East China Sea archipelago to dock at a northern port as long as the ship does not fly the communist China flag.

The vessel, which left Hong Kong on Sunday with 18 Hong Kong activists, 19 crew and 42 reporters on board, ended its mission in tragedy on Thursday when a protest leader died after diving into the water near the islands as a symbolic challenge to Japanese sovereignty there. Protest leader David Chan was the first casualty in a series of campaigns by ethnic Chinese in Taiwan, Hong Kong and China trying to force Japan to give up the islands which Tokyo calls the Senkaku group and China calls the Diaoyus.
The long-simmering dispute erupted in July when Japanese rightwingers built a lighthouse on one of the islands.
"The ship will probably come for docking in the early morning hours on Friday," an official at the northern Keelung port said.

"If they want to dock in order to replenish supplies, repair and rest, I see no problems," another official at the northern Keelung port said by telephone. "However, the ship cannot fly the communist China five-star flag at the front."
A Hong Kong television reporter aboard the Kien Hwa 2 said earlier on Thursday that the ship's captain wanted to sail to Keelung rather than return to Hong Kong following the protest.
Taiwan has banned all direct contacts with China since the two separated after a civil war in 1949, but it typically allows private Chinese vessels to dock for humanitarian assistance.

Taiwan's state-run Central News Agency quoted unnamed navigation officials as saying Taipei would allow Kien Hwa 2 to dock on humanitarian grounds even if it flies China's flag. But the second official contacted at Keelung insisted the flag must not fly at the bow.

"International guidelines do not have any restrictions on what flag a boat may fly or carry. But according to commonly accepted norms and courtesy the only flag that flies at the front should be the flag of the host country," he said.

Chan's group sailed out of Hong Kong last Sunday intending to rip down the lighthouse and Japanese flags and to plant a People's Republic of China red communist flag, claiming the islands as Chinese sovereign territory. Taiwan also claims the archipelago.
Chan's ship was forced to abandon its landing attempt due to stormy seas earlier on Thursday.
